In the 16th century, during the Protestant Reformation, a group of German Christians, known as the Moravians, adopted the name 'Zion' to describe their communal living and religious commitment. They established several settlements, one of which was named 'Zionaria'.

Another reference to the name 'Zionaria' can be found in the 19th century, in the context of the African American community in the United States. 'Zion' was a common name for African American churches and communities, and 'Zionaria' was used to refer to a specific African American female religious organization. This organization was founded in 1852 by a woman named Maria W. Stewart, who was an influential African American abolitionist, poet, and public speaker. The organization's primary focus was on spiritual growth and uplifting the African American community through religious and moral education.
